{"id": "1:6/q20", "question": "What inward journey can the guidance petition describe?", "turns_on": "The seeker's station and whether the route is knowledge, practice, self-effacement or continued ascent.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q20/p1", "position": "For the elect, the path is an unending journey in God after arrival.", "reasons": "Bursevī and al-Ālūsī distinguish arrival from continual ascent through inexhaustible divine manifestations; al-Qāshānī speaks of unity, love and light."}, {"id": "1:6/q20/p2", "position": "It asks to turn toward God, gain gnosis, witness Him and move beyond heedlessness and self-attributes.", "reasons": "Al-Sulamī records distinct seeker, believer and knower stations, direct witnessing, annihilation, and God's care; al-Junayd asks for proper servanthood amid bewilderment."}, {"id": "1:6/q20/p3", "position": "The path is servitude, poverty before God, prophetic practice, or fear and hope.", "reasons": "Reports from Abū Ḥafṣ, Sahl and others offer distinct inward disciplines and images."}, {"id": "1:6/q20/p4", "position": "Rational inquiry and purification are two open routes to guidance.", "reasons": "Rāzī argues that every atom supplies proofs of a wise maker, while spiritual discipline has a distinct path for every seeker."}]}
{"id": "1:6/q21", "question": "What does the petition teach about divine guidance and human agency?", "turns_on": "How divine action relates to disclosure, success, and human choice.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q21/p1", "position": "Guidance can be clarification without compelled success, or a divinely created success.", "reasons": "The sources invoke Thamūd's rejected clarification, the Prophet's inability to guide a loved one, and disputes about divine command, will and creation."}, {"id": "1:6/q21/p2", "position": "Human beings depend on God's continuing aid to reach truth and obey.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī cites the request against Qadarī sufficiency; Rāzī notes persistent disagreement despite effort, and prophets attribute knowledge to God."}, {"id": "1:6/q21/p3", "position": "Human acts are not created by God, or the request for help would be pointless.", "reasons": "Al-Jishumī argues asking for guidance would otherwise resemble asking for one's bodily color."}]}
{"id": "1:6/q22", "question": "How does al-Fātiḥa organize the verse and summarize the Qur'an?", "turns_on": "Which thematic map or structural correspondence explains the verse's place.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q22/p1", "position": "The sura moves from God's praise and lordship through worship and reliance to guidance and the fates of human groups.", "reasons": "The guidance request is the servant's major petition; several authors map it to the sura's last half, prayer acts, spiritual ascent or the Qur'an's central aims."}, {"id": "1:6/q22/p2", "position": "The sura gathers core Qur'anic disciplines and was given a distinctive compact form.", "reasons": "Sources variously count monotheism, law, moral conduct, prophecy, resurrection, promise, warning and stories; al-Ṭabarī cites the Qur'an's inimitable arrangement against the objection that later verses repeat earlier ones."}, {"id": "1:6/q22/p3", "position": "Al-Baqara's Book supplies the requested guidance.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī and al-Zarkashī see its opening as an answer and its groups as examples to follow or avoid."}]}
{"id": "1:6/q23", "question": "What reports and rulings concern reciting al-Fātiḥa in prayer?", "turns_on": "The strength and scope of the obligation and reported virtues.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q23/p1", "position": "Reciting al-Fātiḥa in prayer is obligatory or a pillar.", "reasons": "Rāzī adduces the Prophet's practice, the caliphs, community practice, “no prayer without the Opening,” 73:20, and the sura's comprehensive purposes."}, {"id": "1:6/q23/p2", "position": "Reports describe the sura's recitation, repetition, healing and virtue.", "reasons": "Sources cite the divided-prayer hadith, the greatest-sura report, daily prayer cycles, and healing use."}]}
{"id": "1:6/q24", "question": "How are verse boundaries and pauses around this verse analyzed?", "turns_on": "Whether the boundary or pause is based on count, syntax, semantic completion or recitation practice.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q24/p1", "position": "Verse counts differ over the basmala and the following favored-path clause.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr records regional counts; Burhān discusses a boundary after ihdinā in a report."}, {"id": "1:6/q24/p2", "position": "A pause after “straight” can be acceptable, but beginning with the dependent following phrase is poor.", "reasons": "Al-Zarkashī and Ibn al-Jazarī distinguish complete, sufficient and incomplete pauses and the verbal attachment into 1:7."}]}
{"id": "1:6/q25", "question": "How can the path have multiple valid applications?", "turns_on": "Whether interpretations describe one referent or permit different readings.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q25/p1", "position": "Several glosses can describe qualities or instances of one path.", "reasons": "Sufyān treats many exegetical differences as compatible; al-Suyūṭī and al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī likewise distinguish the shared sense from named instances."}, {"id": "1:6/q25/p2", "position": "Many possible Qur'anic senses require care in disputation.", "reasons": "Abū al-Dardāʾ urges recognizing interpretive aspects; ʿAlī tells Ibn ʿAbbās to debate Kharijites from Sunna because they could exploit Qur'anic multivalence."}]}
{"id": "1:6/q26", "question": "Where was al-Fātiḥa revealed?", "turns_on": "The prayer-history inference and Mujāhid's contrary report.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q26/p1", "position": "Early in Mecca.", "reasons": "The Study Quran reports the majority view and argues early prayer required the sura."}, {"id": "1:6/q26/p2", "position": "In Medina.", "reasons": "The Study Quran attributes this report to Mujāhid."}]}
{"id": "1:6/q27", "question": "What names and virtues of al-Fātiḥa relate to this request?", "turns_on": "Different names emphasize different functions.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q27/p1", "position": "The Opening begins scripture, prayer and other acts.", "reasons": "The Study Quran also says it can open the breast to faith."}, {"id": "1:6/q27/p2", "position": "The Mother of the Book gathers Qur'anic meanings.", "reasons": "The Study Quran connects the title with 3:7 and a celestial archetype."}, {"id": "1:6/q27/p3", "position": "The Seven Oft-Repeated, Cure and Foundation stress repetition, healing and its foundational role.", "reasons": "The first title is linked with 15:87."}]}
{"id": "1:6/q28", "question": "How does seeking Qur'anic knowledge relate to guidance here?", "turns_on": "The Book's breadth, spiritual preparation and transmitted expertise.", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q28/p1", "position": "Guidance to the Book includes learning its knowledge and foundations.", "reasons": "Ibn Masʿūd says to probe the Book; al-Bayhaqī specifies foundations of knowledge."}, {"id": "1:6/q28/p2", "position": "Understanding requires an attentive heart.", "reasons": "Early authorities contrast understanding with arrogance, worldly preoccupation and idleness."}, {"id": "1:6/q28/p3", "position": "The Companions had distinct expertise, especially ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās.", "reasons": "Al-Zarkashī recounts their reputation and other Companions' specialties."}]}
{"id": "1:6/q29", "question": "How does al-Fātiḥa compare with the Lord's Prayer?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "1:6/q29/p1", "position": "Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī judges al-Fātiḥa's prayer more coherent.", "reasons": "He criticizes father-language, political-sounding requests, forgiveness conditioned on another's forgiveness, and asking to avoid life's trials."}]}
